{{Short description|Japanese kind of clothing}}
[[File:Jidai Matsuri 2009 407.jpg|thumb|A woman wearing a red Suikan at a festival.]]
A '''{{nihongo|suikan|水干}}''' is a type of clothing that used to be worn by low-ranking officials serving the imperial court during the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|ceb|Panahon sa Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} (794–1185).<ref name="KDJ" /><ref name="DJR" />  It is generally worn over other clothes.<ref name=":1" /> The word "Suikan" literally means "water-drying,"<ref name="KDJ">R:Kokugo Dai Jiten</ref><ref name="DJR">R:Daijirin</ref> referring to the process of stretching the cloth and drying it without using glue. The clothing is a sliding-door type of jacket with a single-breasted body and open sides, and the collar is tied with a kumihimo cord.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=第２版,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,デジタル大辞泉,旺文社日本史事典 三訂版,世界大百科事典 |title=水干(すいかん)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%B0%B4%E5%B9%B2-82832 |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref>  The term "suikan hakama" is also used to refer to the long [[hakama]] worn with the Suikan, although the exact meaning of this term is somewhat debated.<ref name=":0" /> It is considered a quite formal form of clothing.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Suikan |url=https://ee0r.com/proj/suikan.html |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=ee0r.com}}</ref> It features very large sleeves that attach to the shoulders for a short distance. The garment is made from one very wide fabric panel. The sides are open. This shows the clothes worn underneath.<ref name=":1" />

== Overview ==
Suikan of a single color and plain fabric are used for less formal ones, and for lower ranked people.<ref name=":1" />

They are tied together with knots at the necks and shoulders.<ref name=":1" />

In the late Heian period, various materials were used to make Suikan, including white [[linen]], plain-colored [[cloth]], and [[tie-dye]]d cloth. Warriors who became lower-ranked military officers of the court also wore Suikan, which gradually became a formal attire. From the {{ill|Kamakura period|ar|فترة كاماكورا|be|Перыяд Камакура|bg|Камакура|bn|কামাকুরা যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی کاماکورا|cs|Období Kamakura|de|Kamakura-Zeit|eo|Kamakura-epoko|es|Período Kamakura|et|Kamakura ajastu|eu|Kamakura aroa|fa|دوره کاماکورا|fi|Kamakura-kausi|fr|Époque de Kamakura|gl|Período Kamakura|he|תקופת קמקורה|hu|Kamakura-kor|id|Zaman Kamakura|it|Periodo Kamakura|ja|鎌倉時代|ko|가마쿠라 시대|lt|Kamakura laikotarpis|mn|Камакура эрин|nl|Kamakuraperiode|no|Kamakura-perioden|pt|Período Kamakura|ru|Период Камакура|simple|Kamakura period|sk|Obdobie Kamakura|sl|Obdobje Kamakura|sr|Камакура период|sv|Kamakura|th|ยุคคามากูระ|tl|Panahong Kamakura|tr|Kamakura Dönemi|uk|Період Камакура|vi|Thời kỳ Kamakura|wuu|镰仓时代|zh|鎌倉時代|zh_min_nan|Kamakura sî-tāi|zh_yue|鎌倉時代|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|be|Перыяд Мурамаці|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ceb|Panahon sa Muromachi|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|ilo|Panahon ti Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|kk|Муромачи кезеңі|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, samurai wore Suikan as formal dress along with hunting clothes.<ref name=":0" />

It is made with a single body (no backstitching) with a rounded collar, similar to a hunter's robe. However, the collar is not fastened with a dragonfly, but with a string attached to the back center of the collar and the upper front edge of the collar. The breast and sleeves are decorated with [[chrysanthemum]] ornaments. The long part pierced through is called "oohari," the short part "kohari," and the remainder below is called "dew".<ref>近藤良和、[[平凡社新書]]『装束の日本史』（初版発行2007年1月11日）P164-174。</ref>。

The Suikan was typically worn in the banryo style, but a method was devised to wear it in the tari-kubi style with the collar folded inward. A braided cord was used to reinforce and decorate the garment, and the wearer would typically wear a kuboshi hat and kukuri hakama with the Suikan.<ref name=":0" />

Various materials have been used for making Suikan, such as [[hemp]] cloth, plain [[silk]], [[twill]], and [[gauze]]. Fancier ones are made entirely of silk. The hem of the Suikan is tied together with a braided cord to prevent fraying, and tucked into the [[hakama]].<ref name=":0" />

Some suikan have kikutoji for decoration. They make the clothing stronger at certain points, and are often made of silk yarn. They look like pom-poms that have been flattened by ironing.<ref name=":1" />
